# Pixi tasks

Task-oriented reference for the pixi task surface. Everything is defined in
`pixi.toml`: a task lives under one or more `[feature.<name>.tasks]` tables,
and an environment (`[environments]`) composes a list of features -- a task
is runnable under an environment only when that environment's feature list
includes the feature the task is declared under. This page groups tasks by
their declaring feature and lists, for each feature, every environment that
composes it.

Pass extra args after `--`:

```bash
pixi run -e <env> <task> -- [args]
```

`docs/reference/environments.md` is the environments-first view of the same
`[environments]` table (composed features per environment); this page is
the tasks-first view (environments per feature).

316 tasks across 24 features, as of this render.

## Feature: `bmad-ui`

Environments: `bmad-ui`

| Task | Description |
|---|---|
| `bmad-dashboard-install` | Install the BMAD Dashboard VS Code extension into the local editor (VS Code / Insiders / VSCodium / code-server); --list to confirm, --uninstall to remove |
| `mybmad` | MyBMAD web dashboard launcher: `up` starts (local PostgreSQL + web server on :3002), `stop` stops the DB, `promote-admin --email <you>` grants admin |

## Feature: `conda-smithy`

Environments: `conda-smithy`, `local-recipes`

| Task | Description |
|---|---|
| `lint` | Lint every recipe with the CI-parity conda-smithy (the CalVer 2026.x line the conda-forge webservice runs, solved ephemerally by `pixi exec` because it hard-depends on the `conda` package this env cannot carry -- G65). Passes only directories that hold a recipe.yaml or meta.yaml: `recipes/*` also matches holding dirs (broken-recipes, sample, ...) and the linter aborts the whole run on the first one. Until 2026-09-05 this task ran the env's pinned 3.62.0, which cannot lint a v1 cross-compile `if/then` build block at all (hint_suggest_noarch .startswith on a mapping; recipes/array-record). The --conda-forge mode calls GitHub per recipe through os.environ[GH_TOKEN] (anonymous = 60 req/h, and a corpus this size crawls); the task exports `gh auth token` when GH_TOKEN is unset. Budget an hour for the whole corpus -- pass a single `recipes/<name>` via `conda-smithy recipe-lint --conda-forge recipes/<name>` (G65) for one recipe. |

| `due-for-verification-check` | Batches every tracked planning-artifacts/deferred-work-ledger.md entry (every project) that has never been re-checked against live code (no `verified:` line) or was last checked past the DUE_FOR_VERIFICATION_STALENESS_DAYS staleness threshold (sources/chain.py) — informs only, always WARN, never gates. Every ID'd entry counts regardless of status: (closed/done entries are not exempt). Each due entry is additionally churn-checked: when every code path its ledger text cites (backtick-quoted, excluding `source_spec:`) has had zero git commits since the entry's churn-window start (its `verified:` date, or a derived authoring date when never verified), the SAME finding's evidence is tagged `skip_reason: no-churn` — deprioritized, not resolved; any unresolved or churned path, or zero extractable paths, leaves it fully due (safe default). Each due entry that SURVIVES the churn filter is further offered a mechanical check for ONE grep-recomputable claim shape: a backtick-quoted bare identifier claimed unused/unreferenced/never called/no callers/dead code within 80 characters. `git grep -n -w -I --untracked --no-exclude-standard` (whole repo, including not-yet-committed and gitignored-but-untracked files, excluding every `**/deferred-work-ledger.md` so an entry's own claim text never counts as a call site against itself, excluding the symbol's own `def`/`async def`/`class` line except for any further occurrence of the symbol on that same line) recomputes its live call-site count without an agent, tagging the finding `mechanical_verdict: still-open` (count still 0) or `mechanical_verdict: escalate` (count now nonzero — needs Story 11.4's agent judgment); never `resolved`. A verdict is only asserted when the symbol resolves to a real found declaration — a bare identifier with no `def`/`class` anywhere (e.g. a variable/constant) gets no verdict. No recognizable claim, a churn-skipped entry, an unresolved declaration, or a git failure leaves the finding with no `mechanical_*` keys. Reconcile by re-reading the entry against live code and appending a fresh `verified: <date> — ...` line. Contract: spec-deferred-work-resolution-sweep CAP-1 + CAP-2 + CAP-3. |

Counts come from each station's TRACKED planning-artifacts/sprint-status-ledger.yaml (the twin of the gitignored Tier-3 feed), never from an ad-hoc regex over commit subjects and never from docs/dashboard/data.js, which lags until a merge to main. Running stations are detected live from `marshal status --format json`, so a finished run flips to `complete` on its own rather than rotting in a hardcoded list. |
| `forward-dependency-check` | Detector: a story's own documented **Deps:** names a story in a LATER epic, and bmad-loop cannot see it. `next_actionable` (bmad_loop.sprintstatus) is a strict file-order scan within the current epic with no depends_on concept at all — confirmed against the installed library. A plain `bmad-loop run` would dispatch the forward-dependent story the moment its own epic clears, burning a dev attempt on work that can't complete yet. Found live 2026-08-03 in marshal (2-3 deps S-3.2, 2-7 deps S-4.1, 8-5 deps S-10.2); the fix is the non-standard `blocked` status (the loader does not validate against STORY_STATUSES, same mechanism `optional` relies on), then `python scripts/promote_sprint_status.py`. COVERAGE is keyed on MACHINE-READABLE refs, four classes (reworked 2026-08-08): `measured` (every declaration resolved or explicitly none) · `partial` (a real dependency stated in a grammar DEP_RE cannot parse — the ratio is named, so a station can never read as fully verified; this is how mason reported clean with 0 of 30 declarations parseable) · `no-dispatch` (the ledger positively shows 0 actionable stories, so nothing can be dispatched early — a measured fact, NOT a parse-clean claim) · `unmeasured` (no declaration and work remains, or the ledger is unreadable). Grammar: `S-<epic>.<num>` story, `S-<epic>.*` whole epic, `<station>:S-<epic>.<num>` cross-station, `—` none; prose only as trailing context. Contract: docs/dreams/bmad-loop-forward-dependency-blindness.md + its Spec under pyforge-marshal. |
| `fr-without-cap-check` | Detector: a product requirement minted after the rule date names its source capability (doctor Story 25.2, spec-one-chain-per-station CAP-5; CHAIN-STANDARD § 2 `FR-n <- CAP-m`). New FR/NFR ids per station PRD (vs docs/governance/fr-baseline.json, re-baselined only at that station's fold PR) must cite a CAP-m on the defining line or its first body line -- else FAIL fr-without-cap; a citation no open Spec under the station declares is FAIL fr-cap-unresolved. |
| `frozen-path-changed-check` | Detector: no capability currently rebuilding/moving in the tracked capability ledger (docs/foundry/manifest.{yaml,yml,json}, absent pre-cutover) had one of its own frozen source paths touched by origin/main..HEAD (AD-22's freeze rule). OK when no ledger exists (today's real state, every real invocation until cutover begins). FAIL on a genuine violation, naming the capability and the changed path. |
| `general-docs-consistency-check` | Detector: human-facing documentation identity contradictions (Story 22.3, spec-general-docs-consistency CAP-3). Cross-references station README vs skill-brief and AGENTS.md vs station Dream claims — bounded, textual, evidence-based. Warn-only, read-only, fail-open — never a second PR gate. Contract: spec-22-3-a-repeatable-doctor-detector-catches-this-class-of-drift-going-forward. |
| `governance-currency` | Detector: every skill, script and path named in the governance documents (_bmad-output/EXEMPLAR-STANDARD.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/reference/test-charter.md) still resolves. Story 32.6 / spec-fleet-consistency-standard CAP-6, written because EXEMPLAR-STANDARD spent two BMAD versions naming four skills that had not existed since 6.11 with no gate noticing -- INV-4's argument applied to the prose that governs the detectors. A name resolves as a skill, a script or a pixi task/dependency, all derived from the tree; deliberate historical citations are exempted only by an explicit governance-currency:ignore-start/end marker, never a heuristic. scope=repo. Exit 0 clean / 1 findings / 2 could-not-run. Flags: -- --json, -- --file <path>. |
| `index-freshness-check` | Detector: codegraph and cocoindex indices in loop homes are present and fresh (Story 28.7, SPEC-marshal-token-economy CAP-10). Advisory only: staleness never blocks a run; the findings inform admission decisions. For each loop home, reads its rendered `.bmad-loop/policy.toml`, checks the `[context]` layer declarations, and for each ENABLED layer (structure-graph → codegraph, derived-context → cocoindex), verifies the index is present and its mtime is at or after HEAD's commit timestamp — the same git-timestamp discipline CAP-13 requires for graph-node staleness. If git cannot report HEAD (not a repo, no commits, no git binary), freshness is not evaluated; presence alone reports OK. scope=runtime (loop homes live in ~/.bmad-loops, a gitignored Tier-3 directory), excluded from detectors-ci. |
| `ledger-direction-check` | Detector: the tracked sprint ledger versus git merge history, WITH DIRECTION (marshal FR-137/FR-138). `landed-but-unpromoted` — merge history names a story the ledger has not marked done — is the FAIL half and the incident this exists for. `done-but-unmerged` is advisory (WARN, never reds the run): a done flip absent from the ledger at the base ref AND unnamed by any merge subject. Both read git only, never the gitignored Tier-3 sprint-status.yaml — a statement of intent is not evidence of landing. |
| `ledger-regression-check` | Detector: no commit un-finishes a story in a tracked sprint ledger. The OUTERMOST of three guards on the same failure: promote_sprint_status.py refuses the write, --project bounds the blast radius, and this compares two TRACKED files across a revision range so it holds even when those are bypassed, hand-edited, or --allow-regression-ed. Reads only the tracked twin via git show, so it runs in bare CI where the gitignored Tier-3 feeds are invisible — the asymmetry that let one sync destroy 96 `done` markers across four stations on 2026-08-08 while printing success. `done` is the only guarded state; reopening a story is legitimate but must be its own commit. Compares origin/main..HEAD. |
| `lint-types` | Story 66.1 / 66.2: the whole hygiene lane in one task -- exactly what .github/workflows/lint-types.yml runs and what pr-preflight's `lint-types` leg runs. |
| `live-proof-surface-check` | Detector: a touched surface catalogued in live-proof-surfaces.md gets an advisory finding naming it (Story 26.1, spec-pyforge-doctor CAP-77). Matches ONLY the catalog's hand-authored Surface globs column against origin/main..HEAD -- never a keyword pulled from prose (the first attempt's substring fallback matched unrelated real files; amended 2026-09-20). Quotes the catalog's own 'how to prove it live' cell verbatim, including the atlas Chromium/DuckDB/WASM row's honest named gap. Warn-only, read-only, fail-open -- never a second PR gate. |
| `llms-full-check` | Detector: report drift between docs/reference/library-llms-full.md (the library catalog) and pixi.toml — undocumented deps, ghost entries, version-floor drift. Exits non-zero on drift. Reconciler = the regeneration prompt in the catalog header. Pass -- --json for machine output. |
| `loop-stall-check` | Watchdog: a live bmad-loop run has stopped making progress. `bmad-loop status` reports the last phase it WROTE, so a session blocked on an interactive startup dialog reads `dev-running` forever — and the dialog never reaches the session log, it renders only in the tmux pane, so the log just stops growing. The supervisor's stall ladder does not fire either. Live cost 2026-07-31: scribe 1.3 sat 74 min on the CLAUDE.md external-import dialog, seven times its 600s grace, while five siblings wrote every second. Compares now against the newest mtime across a run's logs + journal, for runs whose state.json says neither finished, stopped, paused, nor parked-only (a paused run is SUPPOSED to sit still, and since Story 25.5 a parked-only run — every task awaiting-operator — reports awaiting-operator (run bmad-loop confirm) and exits 0 instead of reading as a stall). Threshold 15m, override with -- --minutes N. Catches any cause: folder-trust prompt, external-import prompt, wedged model call, hung nested CLI. Contract: spec-bmad-loop-governance. |
| `mason-cfe-surface-check` | Detector (FR-45/AD-15): Mason (src/shared/packages/pyforge-mason/**) never modifies the conda-forge-expert surface (.claude/skills/conda-forge-expert/**, .claude/scripts/conda-forge-expert/**, .claude/tools/conda_forge_server.py). Scans every commit touching the mason path (derived range, no hardcoded baseline) and flags any non-sanctioned one that also touches CFE — exactly one exception is allowed: a commit whose subject starts `retro:` AND whose diff includes the CFE CHANGELOG.md (subject alone never launders a CFE touch); a second such commit is itself a finding (`exception-reused`). scope=repo — reads tracked commit history only. Exits non-zero on any finding. Pass -- --json for machine output. Contract: _bmad-output/projects/pyforge-mason/planning-artifacts (Story 5.2). |
| `memlog-fidelity-check` | Harness: inventory every spec SPEC.md and architecture ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md across the eight stations; verify sibling .memlog.md exists; optionally diff scratch bmad-spec/bmad-architecture re-derives against live rendered files (--compare SCRATCH). Reconcile by memlog append then headless re-derive (see --invoke-hints). Contract: spec-44-13-memlog-fidelity / fnd:AD-20. |
| `missing-preserve-check` | Watchdog: an intent-gap halt left no preserve artifact (Story 20.5 / CAP-3 of spec-bmad-loop-intent-gap-work-preservation). Story 20.4 parks attempt-preserve/* or failed/<story>/changes.patch before the halt reverts; if that seam is bypassed or upstream shifts, the halt still looks clean while the attempt is gone. Scans marshal journals under ~/.bmad-loops for escalation-detected (intent-gap reason) or intent-gap-preserve-failed; trips when no preserve branch/patch is present. scope=runtime (excluded from detectors-ci), same placement as loop-stall-check / baseline-drift-check — NOT pyforge.doctor.sources. Never imports bmad_loop. Contract: spec-20-5-missing-preserve-detector. |
| `mypy` | Story 66.1 (spec-pyforge-steward CAP-153): `mypy -p pyforge.<station>` inside each of the ten pyforge-* packages, each read with its own [tool.mypy] (strict for pyforge-core). The CI lane and pr-preflight call this task verbatim. |
| `pixi-currency-staleness-check` | Detector: the Dream's four pixi dependency ledgers have not fallen behind pixi.toml's own commit history (Story 21.7, spec-pixi-candidate-currency CAP-4). Warn-only, read-only, fail-open — advisory ledger staleness, never a second PR gate. Contract: spec-21-7-the-pixi-candidate-ledgers-get-their-staleness-check. |
| `pixi-version-check` | Detector: every pixi-version pin site (CI workflows, both Containerfiles, environment.yaml, pixi.toml's own feature floors) agrees with pixi.toml's requires-pixi floor. Registry lives in scripts/pixi_version_registry.py, not a hand-maintained comment — that comment drifted three times before this existed, most recently 2026-08-21 when a pixi upgrade left 10 external sites stale and one (src/platform/compose/dbgpt/Containerfile) unregistered entirely, breaking container-dbgpt CI. Reconciler: bump-pixi-version. Pass -- --json for machine output. |
| `platform-ci-local` | Replay Platform CI (.github/workflows/platform-ci.yml) locally — the test job step for step, the three image builds, the container job's runtime smokes, and golden-path-promotion + the deploy verifier — against an ephemeral PostgreSQL 17/Redis 7 from platform-dev. Zero Actions minutes. Stages: --test --images --container --promotion (default all); --engine podman. Docker or podman on the host. |
| `platform-ci-test-requirements-check` | Detector (Story 16.1 / CAP-5): src/platform/requirements/{base,local,production}.txt stay retired — pixi.toml is the sole platform dep authority. Exits non-zero if those files are resurrected. Pass -- --json for machine output. |
| `platform-policy-suite-check` | Detector: src/platform's manifest-only tests/policy subset (retro action item 3, 2026-09-04) — catches a pixi.toml regression like the openfeature-provider-flagd/cachebox ceiling drop even when Platform CI itself is disabled. Shells out to the platform-ci-test pixi env's own interpreter (WARN, not FAIL, if that env is not installed here — install it with `pixi install -e platform-ci-test` to make this a real gate). Exits non-zero only on an actual policy-suite failure. |
| `pr-preflight` | Run locally, before pushing, everything a PR to rxm7706/local-recipes actually gates on. One command, so a green local run means a green CI run.  Covers the four lanes that red a PR: `detectors-ci` (the CI detector subset), `test-ci` (the CFE regression suite — this is the lane that owns the spec-surface meta-test), `pyforge-station-tests` (pyforge-core + all 8 station suites, which ALL fire together on any shared-surface change), and `pyforge-station-coverage-gates` (the touched-module coverage floors).  Added 2026-09-14 after PR #1355 went red on two lanes that had NO local equivalent: `cfe-regression-net` failed on a stale spec-surface baseline (a scoped `--write-baseline` had been taken, then a governed file was edited again, silently invalidating it), and `named-module-gates (doctor)` failed on a coverage floor that only measures modules a branch touches — so it had been latent for weeks and surfaced on an unrelated edit. Neither was reachable from `detectors` or `pyforge-station-tests`.  NOT covered (needs Docker/podman or a live service): the container/guild-container jobs, atlas's Chromium/DuckDB/WASM setup, herald's browser check, and scribe's Postgres+pgvector service (`scribe-pg-up` first, or scribe's durable GraphStore tests error).  Runs from `-e pyforge-guild` (the session default) as well as `-e local-recipes`: the `test-ci` leg is pinned to `local-recipes` because the CFE regression suite is a factory task that lives only there (found 2026-09-16, steward Story 63.1 -- the first `pr-preflight` from the Guild env failed with "could not find the task 'test-ci'"), the same per-leg pinning the two station aggregates already use. Fifth leg added the same day: `scripts-suite` (`tests/scripts`, the detectors.yml job `pyforge-doctor-scripts-test` in `-e pyforge-ci`) redded PR #1388 on a test that pinned a task to `feature.local-recipes` -- a CI lane this aggregate did not cover, the very gap it exists to close. Sixth leg added 2026-09-18 (herald Story 24.2, spec-pyforge-herald CAP-49, closes DW-FU-23-5): `site-check` (`-e site`) mirrors the new `docsite-check.yml` `pull_request` lane -- until then no `pr-preflight` leg, and no PR-gating CI lane at all, ran `docsite/build.py`, so a broken family-page template could merge with every gate green. Seventh leg added 2026-09-20 (doctor Story 30.2 review pass): `docs-map-render-test` -- a `tests/scripts/` file needing jsonschema (unavailable in `pyforge-ci`, which `pyforge-doctor-scripts-test` already covers for the stdlib-only subset) needs its OWN leg here rather than silently only ever skipping. Eighth leg added 2026-09-24 (doctor Story 30.3, spec-pyforge-doctor CAP-84): `docs-gen-test` -- the five reference-page generators import PyYAML via `_docs_gen_common.py`, not a declared `pyforge-ci` dependency (each test file skips cleanly there via `pytest.importorskip` if that ever stops being transitively available), so this gets its own leg rather than relying on `pyforge-doctor-scripts-test`. |
| `precommit-config-check` | Story 66.2 (spec-pyforge-steward CAP-154): .pre-commit-config.yaml exists at the repo root, declares the commit-msg and pre-push hook types, and carries the two local hooks (commit-msg attribution refusal; pre-push pr-preflight). Exit 0 clean, 1 findings. |
| `pyforge-station-coverage-gates` | Run every station's CI-mirroring coverage gate (scripts/coverage_gates_ci.py, touched modules, 80% unit floor) in its own pixi env — the local twin of .github/workflows/coverage-gates.yml's `named-module-gates` matrix. Declarative depends-on, never a shell loop (pixi's task shell cannot parse one; see pyforge-station-tests). |
| `pyforge-station-tests` | Run pyforge-core's suite + every PyForge station's own pytest suite locally, mirroring .github/workflows/pyforge-station-tests.yml's core-test + per-station jobs — the exact set that ALL fire together whenever pixi.toml/pixi.lock/pyforge-core/pyforge-testing-kit changes (that workflow's shared-surface rule), which is easy to miss since most day-to-day PRs only touch one station and never see this combination locally. Added 2026-09-14 after a 5-day GitHub Actions billing outage let ~260 PRs merge with this workflow never actually running; a pixi.toml dep bump was the first push afterward to touch shared surface, and it surfaced 5 days of accumulated drift (doctor/marshal/mason) all at once. The pyforge-core leg (Story 52.2, spec-pyforge-core CAP-8) runs FIRST: it is the cheapest (~10 s) and fails fastest, and its sole-ownership meta-tests scan every station's tree, so a station-only change can red it. Fails fast (first red leg stops the run) and covers only pyforge-core's `pyforge-core-test` plus each station's own `pyforge-<station>-test` task — NOT atlas's Chromium/DuckDB/WASM setup, herald's browser check, scribe's Postgres+pgvector service (see `scribe-pg-up`), or the separate guild-container job; run those stations' own CI-mirroring steps first if you touched them. Run this before pushing any pixi.toml/pixi.lock/pyforge-core/pyforge-testing-kit change. |
| `retired-console-check` | FR-7 / Story 30.2: fail if the retired Guildhall generator, data.js, or the four dashboard-gen/watch/check/drift pixi tasks are reintroduced. Kedro-Viz is out of scope. |
| `ruff` | Story 66.1 (spec-pyforge-steward CAP-153): `ruff check` over the ten src/shared/packages/pyforge-*/ packages (src + tests), each read with its own [tool.ruff]. The CI lane and pr-preflight call this task verbatim. |
| `ruff-format` | Story 66.1 (spec-pyforge-steward CAP-153): `ruff format --check` over the ten pyforge-* packages. Fix with `pixi run -e pyforge-guild ruff-format-fix`. |
| `ruff-format-fix` | Story 66.1: mutator twin of `ruff-format` -- rewrites files in place. Never in CI. |
| `scribe-graph-freshness-check` | Detector (Story 8.1, spec-8-1): the compiled scribe knowledge graph (.claude/data/pyforge-scribe/graph.json) is fresh -- its mtime is no older than the nightly trigger's own 24h period (pyforge-scribe-nightly-compile.timer). Advisory only: never a PR gate, never a second verdict alongside the detector set's existing gates -- proof the nightly trigger fired, nothing more. Missing graph.json (never compiled, or the trigger was never installed) is its own advisory finding, not an error. scope=runtime (a gitignored, host-local derived artifact a CI runner never populates), excluded from detectors-ci. |
| `spec-surface-check` | Detector: every tracked file is governed by a spec surface: manifest or explicitly allowlisted (scripts/spec_surface_allowlist.txt), and no governed file drifted without its spec's memlog moving. Exits non-zero on findings. Reconcile: update the spec (bmad-spec re-derive). Contract: spec-regenerable-factory CAP-3. |
| `sprint-ledger-query` | Pluggable estate sprint ledger query CLI duty (Story 65.1, spec-pyforge-steward CAP-146..149). Reads each station's TRACKED planning-artifacts/sprint-status-ledger.yaml + epics.md; counts agree with fleet_scan.parse_sprint_status. --format: markdown (default), summary, json, table; flag-gated: sync-matrix/jira-csv/github-json (enable_jira_github_matrix), herald-facts (enable_herald_facts), atlas-dataset (enable_vizro_dataset), static-dossier (enable_dossier_export) -- open one with `-- --flag <name>=true`, FLAGS_<NAME>=true, or .steward/flags.json. stdout carries the payload only; `--output PATH` writes it to that file instead (stdout empty). Writes into no other station's tree by default. |
| `sprint-ledger-sync` | Promote each project's Tier-3 story-status map to its TRACKED twin at planning-artifacts/sprint-status-ledger.yaml. implementation-artifacts/ is gitignored wholesale, so sprint-status.yaml is invisible to CI. Written in the feed's own shape so fleet_scan.parse_sprint_status reads both. Idempotent; run it when a story lands, then commit. |
| `status-body-consistency-check` | Detector: terminal-tier Dream/Spec bodies contradict their declared status (Story 21.12–21.16, spec-status-body-consistency CAP-1..5). Progress phrases, open-questions/memlog drift, measured promissory language, and status-comment/ledger contradictions — warn-only, read-only, fail-open. Surfaces beside dream-vocab and spec-status-missing in one detectors run and fleet-picture ATTENTION. Contract: spec-21-16-the-status-body-check-renders-where-the-operator-already-looks. |
| `story-status-check` | Detector: no story reads `done` in a sprint feed without having landed. A bmad-loop dev pass self-marks its story `done`; if the REVIEW then fails to converge the story is deferred and NOTHING rolls the feed back — a false green in the artifact the dashboard renders and the next run dispatches from, so the board over-reports AND the next run SKIPS a story that was never finished. Caught 3 live on 2026-07-31 (marshal 1-6, doctor 1-4, mason 1-3), all in the same shape: dev completed, review failed. Confirms a landing via a merge commit on any ref OR a harness-recorded commit_sha (AD-33: git owns repository facts), and reports only when the harness positively says deferred/escalated — so hand-implemented stories with no run record are never flagged. The real fix belongs upstream in bmad-loop; this is the containment. Premise note (2026-08-22): BMAD 6.11's build-auto finalize writes `done` only at true finalize (post-review), shrinking — not closing — the dev-marks-done window; pre-6.11 feeds and interrupted runs keep the premise live, so detector behavior is unchanged. Contract: spec-regenerable-factory. |
| `target-version-check` | Story 66.1 (spec-pyforge-steward CAP-153): every pyforge-* package's [tool.ruff] target-version and [tool.mypy] python_version match the interpreter pinned in pixi.toml (the registry shape of pixi-version-check). Exit 0 clean, 1 drift, 2 could-not-run. |
| `unpushed-work-check` | Detector: no work exists only on this disk — local branches carrying unique content that are on no remote, plus dangling commits holding real work that `git gc` may collect without warning. scope=runtime and deliberately NOT in CI: a runner has neither local branches nor dangling objects, so this check would pass vacuously there, which is a false green of the purest kind. Live cost 2026-07-31 when nothing checked: six station loop branches, ~5,150 lines on recover/*, herald 1.2's 734-line transport story (spec included) unpushed for six days, 156 dangling commits, and marshal 1.8's 1,748 lines committed 40 minutes earlier. Flags: -- --branches-only (skip the fsck scan), -- --min-files N, -- --json. Contract: docs/dreams/fidelity-enforcement.md. The standing signal for between-runs staleness now that the standalone interval-push watcher is retired (Story 4.15/FR-177): S-3.10's tip comparison already covers `loop/*` station branches. |

## Feature: `platform-object-storage`

Environments: `platform-object-storage`

| Task | Description |
|---|---|
| `platform-object-storage-down` | Stop the local object-storage server for the selected backend (PYFORGE_OBJECT_STORAGE_BACKEND). The data directory survives, so the next -up starts rather than re-initialises. |
| `platform-object-storage-status` | Report whether the selected backend's local object-storage server is listening on 127.0.0.1:9000. Read-only; always exits 0 (except Garage's clean Windows refusal). |
| `platform-object-storage-up` | Start a real local S3-compatible object-storage server -- Silo (default) or Garage (PYFORGE_OBJECT_STORAGE_BACKEND=garage) -- on the fixed contract endpoint 127.0.0.1:9000. Idempotent: re-running against a live server re-asserts (prints ready) rather than restarting it. Server state lives under gitignored var/platform-object-storage/<backend>/. Garage refuses cleanly on Windows (no win-64 build) rather than silently no-op'ing. |

Requires a caller-supplied PASSING health-screen verdict (--verdict pass + non-empty --abandonment-signal/--license-clarity) on EVERY call; gates eligibility on the row's tier (1/2) directly, never on a not_on_cf boolean. Runs from the atlas project root (kedro CLI needs the project cwd). --no-browser so it works headless; open the printed localhost URL. |
| `viz-build` | Epic 12/FR-62: static `kedro viz build` of the REAL atlas DAG (never the stub-mirror prototype) -> build/api + build/index.html. Wipes any prior build/ first -- kedro-viz's own LocalDeployer only mkdir's the build dir, it never clears stale content, so a node/dataset removed from a real DAG change would otherwise leave its old file behind forever across repeated local invocations (CI's own fresh-checkout-per-run makes this moot there, but a clean slate here removes the gap everywhere). PYTHONHASHSEED=0 is NOT decorative: kedro-viz's static export enumerates nodes/pipelines/edges from internal Python `set`s, whose iteration order CPython randomizes per-process by default (a per-run string-hash seed) -- pinning the seed makes that enumeration order reproducible across runs, which `viz-publish-stage`'s normalize-then-diff pipeline depends on to tell a real DAG change from build noise. |
| `viz-publish-stage` | Epic 12/FR-62: normalize the just-built `build/` output (strips the checkout-anchored absolute path baked into ~53 file-backed dataset nodes under build/api/nodes/*, and fixes the literal build-timestamp in build/api/deploy-viz-metadata -- see tools/normalize_viz_build.py) THEN stages it to docs/dashboard/kedro-viz/, replacing whatever was there. Depends on viz-build so a failed build never stages stale/partial output. |

| `pyforge-steward-coverage-gate` | Mirror of .github/workflows/coverage-gates.yml's `named-module-gates (steward)` job: run scripts/coverage_gates_ci.py over the modules THIS branch touches, in steward's own env, against the 80% unit floor. Distinct from pyforge-steward-test-coverage, which measures named modules against seeded ratchet floors -- this one measures only touched modules and is the gate that actually reds a PR. Added 2026-09-14 after PR #1355: board.py had sat at 70.1% since the Guildhall console was retired, and because the gate only measures TOUCHED modules it stayed invisible until an unrelated edit to that file surfaced it in CI with no local equivalent to catch it first. |
| `pyforge-steward-dogfood` | Steward dogfoods itself: run the CLI from the built env, then run its own drift audit against this repo's current state (Story 1.6). |
| `pyforge-steward-guild-image-build` | Build the root Containerfile and run post-build container gates (Story 48.10; needs docker or podman). |
| `pyforge-steward-test` | Run the pyforge-steward suite across all three tiers (unit + conformance + meta). |
| `pyforge-steward-test-coverage` | Story 32.7 (spec-pyforge-testing-charter CAP-4): full-package named-module coverage evaluate for pyforge-steward. Floors are SEEDED FROM MEASUREMENT and ratchet upward only -- nobody had ever measured this station before 2026-09-07, so a flat 80/70 would have redded the fleet on day one. Fails naming each module under its floor, never a bare percentage. |
| `sprint-ledger-postgres-sync` | Mint Work Passport UUIDs and sync estate sprint ledger items to PostgreSQL / Django ORM (Story 65.1; WorkPassport model, migration 0002). Lives in the pyforge-steward feature -- the one env with both django ([dashboard] extra) and the steward CLI -- NOT in guild-tasks, where it could only ever refuse (no env carrying guild-tasks has django; found at PR #1507's review). Flag-gated: pass `-- --flag enable_postgres_sync=true` (or FLAGS_ENABLE_POSTGRES_SYNC=true), else it refuses with exit 1; needs DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE set, else `refused` on stderr, exit 1 -- never a silent exit-0 no-op. |

## Feature: `scribe-pg`

Environments: `pyforge-scribe-pg`

| Task | Description |
|---|---|
| `scribe-pg-down` | Stop the per-user scribe PostgreSQL cluster (fast shutdown). The data directory survives, so the next scribe-pg-up starts rather than re-initialises. |
| `scribe-pg-status` | Report whether the scribe PostgreSQL cluster is listening on 127.0.0.1:5433 and whether its data directory exists. Read-only; always exits 0. |
| `scribe-pg-up` | Start the per-user PostgreSQL+pgvector cluster pyforge-scribe's durable GraphStore tests require, on 127.0.0.1:5433 with database `scribe_graph` -- the DSN tests/unit/conftest.py hard-codes. Idempotent: re-running against a live cluster re-asserts the database and extension rather than failing. Cluster state lives under gitignored var/scribe-pg/, never a container. |

## Feature: `vuln-db`

Environments: `vuln-db`

| Task | Description |
|---|---|
| `atlas-phase` | Run a single cf_atlas phase from the vuln-db env (use for Phase G / G' which need the vdb library). Same CLI as the local-recipes version. |
| `build-cf-atlas` | Build the conda-forge atlas FROM THE VULN-DB ENV — runs Phase G (vdb summary) which needs the AppThreat vdb library importable. Set PHASE_GP_ENABLED=1 to also run Phase G' (per-version vuln scoring). All other phases run too; TTL gates keep them cheap. |
| `detail-cf-atlas` | Detail card with --vdb on by default (multi-source vulnerability summary: NVD + GHSA + OSV + Snyk + npm + …); add --version VER to scope the affecting-set to an arbitrary release. Pass --no-vdb to skip the vuln pass for a faster card. |
| `detail-cf-atlas-vdb` | Detail card with --vdb --vdb-all preset; pass <name> [--version VER] to list every CVE affecting a specific release (verbose variant of detail-cf-atlas) |
| `inventory-channel` | Inventory a channel/mirror (conda repodata.json \| PyPI Simple v1 \| npm registry \| crates.io). Auto-detects format. --with-vulns ON by default for conda, OFF for others. JFrog auth via env vars. --diff for upstream comparison, --health for mirror signals, --sbom for SBOM. |
| `scan-project` | Scan a project's manifests (pixi.lock, pixi.toml, Cargo.lock/toml, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, environment.yml, Containerfile/Dockerfile) for CVEs. Use --github URL or local path. Add --os for OS-package lookups, --brief for summary, --sbom {cyclonedx,spdx} for SBOM output. |
| `vdb-refresh` | Build/refresh the AppThreat multi-source vulnerability DB (~5-10 min first time, ~600MB at .claude/data/conda-forge-expert/vdb/). Sources: OSV + GHSA. NOTE on KEV: --cache-os was evaluated for DW13 to add AquaSource (which carries NVD + distro CVEs), but appthreat-vulnerability-db's aqua.py hardcodes `kevc` (CISA KEV) into DEFAULT_IGNORE_SOURCE_PATTERNS with no env-var override, so --cache-os would download ~33 GB and still leave vuln_kev_affecting_current=0. KEV is therefore pulled out-of-band via `fetch-cisa-kev` (Path C; <1 MB direct from cisa.gov) and Phase G / G' overlay the result onto vdb's per-CVE output. |
